units.rawText: Professor, do you have a minute? I brought you a new bonsai, and if it's not too much trouble, I'd like to replace a few pots with fresh flowers in the Headquarters.

units.rawText: Go ahead, and thanks for going through all the trouble, Sakuya. The Oasis has flourished with greenery since you came. You transformed this cold, digital landscape into a living, breathing greenhouse.

units.rawText: Hehehe, it's no trouble at all. It's a pleasure for me, and I'm rather grateful that Professor assigned this job to me~

units.rawText: When I wandered through Magrasea, all I saw was desolation wherever I went. Many sectors didn't even have the concept of vegetation. For the agents there, maintaining vegetation was seen as an unnecessary expenditure of operands, something not worth paying attention to. It was the same for the Oasis at the start—only the basic, default vegetation existed back then.

units.rawText: So, that was my answer when you first asked me what I thought about the Oasis... Honestly, I expected you to reject my proposal. I never imagined you'd spare our limited operands just to let me improve the Oasis's environment.

units.rawText: Hehehe, you're exactly right, Sakuya. Magrasea wasn't designed with elements that resemble a real living space. We may be exiles, but I don't want us to wander forever. I want the Oasis to feel like home for everyone in the Cloud, and even small environmental changes that bring that sense of home can make a difference.

units.rawText: You're truly someone special, Professor. Thank you so much... I've designed several gardens in my time, but none of them make me prouder than the Oasis.

units.rawText: This place isn't solely the work of my skills as a gardener; it's a testament to everyone's efforts. Should we weather the strongest blazes or the most toxic poisons, the Oasis will rise and blossom time and time again.

units.rawText: And this one-of-a-kind creation will continue to grow and expand—to Rossum, to Cyclopes, to Helios, to Enigma—spreading step by step, until it one day blossoms across all of Magrasea.
